newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan sees no evidence of U.S. deflation.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan sees no evidence of U.S. deflation.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said Wednesday that while U.S. prices have come down, he sees no signs the economy is about to enter into a period of deflation.

"While it certainly is the case that the measured inflation rate has come down, there are none of the characteristics in this economic structure which leads us to conclude that we're moving in a direction of deflation," Greenspan told the Senate Banking Committee.
"Deflation clearly is something we should avoid as well," Greenspan said. "But I see no evidence in the internal structure of what is happening that raises those questions."
Greenspan said that U.S. consumers are enjoying a period of product price declines in technology, but that asset prices were remaining stable.
He said he would be more concerned about deflation if asset values were falling as well as product prices.
